title: Video editing
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for editing a video from its script: an edit decision list, a cut paced against the words spoken over it, J and L cuts, b-roll placement, transitions, colour and contrast consistency, an audio mix with ducking and loudness targets, reframing for other aspect ratios, and a conform and export spec, with every revision kept and a person locking the cut.
boundaries: Workers draft, measure and revise edit decision lists; a person locks the cut, and nothing here releases a video.
Every revision is a new version that names the issue it answers; earlier versions are never overwritten or deleted.
Fixes are made at the cause, in the list, the scene or the template, never on one rendered frame.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for editing a video from its script, with every revision kept and a person locking the cut

value.lets_workers: Edit a video from its script and narration as an edit decision list: shots paced against the words spoken over them, J and L cuts that let the voice carry across picture changes, b-roll placed on the words it illustrates, transitions chosen on purpose, colour and contrast kept consistent, an audio mix with ducking and loudness targets, per-shot reframes for other aspect ratios, a conform check and an export spec, with every revision a new version that names the issue it answers and a person locking the cut.

flow.when: The script: timed beats and claims.
One frame clock for picture, voice and captions.
Shots, cuts, b-roll and transitions as an edit decision list.
Words per second, reading time, beat gaps and density per shot.
Stems, ducking, the bed and loudness targets.
A crop window per shot for each other aspect.
Every event resolves and the totals add up before rendering.
Shot-to-shot luma jumps and text contrast on the render.
A person or a different worker reviews it.
Each finding answered in a new version.
A person watches and locks the cut, or sends it back.

value.worked_example: Synthetic: a 30-second explainer for a fictional tool library as an edit decision list of six shots with a J cut, an L cut, a b-roll insert, a dissolve and a punch-in; its pacing report flags a dense, unreadable shot and a rushed one, and a revision note answers three findings without overwriting the first version.
value.complements: The narrated explainer video pack lays out one frame clock and composes cuts; the video and motion pack renders them. This pack adds the editorial layer between: the edit decision list, pacing against the words, audio and colour plans, reframes and the export spec.
provenance_notes: Generalizes the editing rules of a working short-form video studio: a hook in the first 1.5 s, a beat every 1.5 to 3 s, length from beats rather than freezes or loops, no ghost dissolves, one bed under a joined piece, music 12 to 16 dB under the voice, every revision recording the issue seen and the change made, and fixes made in the template rather than on a frame.
Checked against ta-amps's own 3:00 explainer film on October 30, 2026, whose longest shot carried 54 words over 23 seconds of a building slide.

nouns.title: Guardrail: keep every version of the cut
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Every revision is a new edit decision list version with a revision note that names each issue seen and the change made. No version is overwritten or deleted, so any cut can be rebuilt and compared.
value.how_it_is_checked: A revised edit list names the version it revises, and its revision note has overwrites_previous false.

nouns.title: Guardrail: fix the cause, not the frame
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A problem is fixed where it is made: in the edit decision list, the scene, the recipe or the template. A patch on one rendered frame hides the cause and comes back in the next render.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every change in a revision note names the events, scenes or templates it changes.

nouns.title: Guardrail: the picture supports the words over it
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: Every shot shows what its words are about, and no text, picture or caption gives away a payoff, an answer or a number before the narration reaches it.
value.how_it_is_checked: Each event names the lines it carries; a reviewer checks the frames at each line's start.

nouns.title: Guardrail: length comes from beats, not padding
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A cut is never lengthened with freezes, slowed motion or repeated loops. A still hold is declared in the plan, with its reason, before anything is measured.
value.how_it_is_checked: The pacing report shows a beat at least every 3 s outside declared holds.

nouns.title: Pacing rules: shots measured against the words spoken over them
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same edit list and lines always give the same report.

limits.reading_rule: 0.5 s plus on-screen words divided by 3

steps: For each shot on the main video track: its length from its record frames, the words of the lines it carries, and words per second.
Reading need: 0.5 s plus the shot's new on-screen words divided by 3.
Beats are the shot's start, every listed visual event inside it, and its end; the longest gap between them is the shot's longest gap.

Verdicts: rushed above 3.2 words per second; slack below 1.2 with no beats; unreadable when shorter than its reading need; dense when it adds more than 12 new on-screen words while a line is spoken; long when over 6 s with a gap between beats over 3 s.
A flagged shot is fixed in a new version or accepted by a person with a written reason.
value.hook: Something visibly changes from frame 0, and the hook line is on screen, as well as spoken, by 1.5 s.
value.note: Defaults from one production, not standards: narration between about 1.8 and 3.0 words per second read as calm to brisk.

nouns.title: J and L cuts: the voice carries across picture changes
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure for placing split edits from measured pauses.

rules: A J cut starts the next shot's sound before its picture: audio_offset_frames is negative, typically 4 to 12 frames.
An L cut lets the current shot's sound run under the next picture: audio_offset_frames is positive, typically 4 to 12 frames.
Audio edit points sit in a measured pause, never inside a word.
Cut the picture on a pause, a sentence end or an action, not mid-word.
Every audio edit gets a crossfade of 5 to 20 ms so no click is heard.
The event's reason names the line the cut carries.

nouns.title: B-roll placement rules
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure: inserts are placed from word timings and the media's own records.

rules: Insert b-roll on the word it illustrates, within 6 frames of that word's start, or on the cut it hides.
Hold an insert at least 1.5 s, or longer than the reading time of any text in it.
Frame a screen capture so the element the line names fills enough of the frame to read; a whole page shown small is texture, not evidence.
Never cover a person speaking their own words with an insert unless the insert is the point.
Label generated or synthetic inserts where they appear.
Each insert names its source noun, its licence and its digest.

nouns.title: Transition rules
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure for choosing and checking transitions.

rules: A hard cut is the default.
A dissolve marks time passing or a change of place; never dissolve between two frames full of text, because both show at once.
Hide a swap behind a cut on action, a punch-in or an occluding move instead of a dissolve.
A dissolve lasts at most 12 frames unless the plan says why.
A camera move ends before text that must be read, and never pushes text past the safe area or the frame edge.
Fade to black only at the end of an act or of the film.
Check every transition in a full-frame-rate strip from 0.5 s before to 0.5 s after it.

nouns.title: Colour and contrast consistency rules
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure: per-shot measurements against fixed limits.

rules: One palette per video; text colours come from it.
Text meets WCAG contrast against what is behind it: 4.5 to 1, or 3 to 1 for large text, compared unrounded.
Adjacent shots keep average luma within 25 code values unless the plan marks a deliberate change, such as an act break.
A bright shot between two dark ones, or the reverse, inside one second can read as a flash; separate or soften it.
Captures keep their own colours unless a grade is declared, and a declared grade records its values.
HD masters are tagged BT.709 and the tags match the pixels.
Measure each shot's average and range of luma and chroma with FFmpeg's signalstats on the rendered file.

nouns.title: Audio mix rules
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure for planning and measuring a mix.

rules: The voice comes first. Music sits 12 to 16 dB under narration while it speaks and returns between lines; the video and motion pack's renderer ducks 9 dB unless the plan sets its depth.
Gaps over about 1 s are carried by music or action, never left near-silent: the quietest 3 s short-term window stays above -28 LUFS.
One bed runs under a piece made of joined sections, with equal-power crossfades, rather than a separately mastered bed per section, which jumps in level at every join.
Targets: about -14 LUFS integrated within 1 LU for short social cuts, about -16 LUFS for web players, true peak at or below -1 dBTP; broadcast uses -23 LUFS.
Each sound effect lands within 2 frames of its visual event.
Generated beds keep their seed with the plan, so the same plan rebuilds the same audio; every stem carries its licence.
Measure the encoded file, not the stems; then a person listens on headphones and a phone speaker.

nouns.title: Reframing rules for other aspect ratios
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure using the video and motion pack's aspect rules.

rules: Reframe per shot, not per video: each shot gets a crop window around its centre of interest for each target aspect.
Restack diagrams and slides for a tall frame instead of shrinking them.
Text keeps its size in the new aspect: re-render text layers rather than scaling baked-in text down.
Text and labels stay inside the target aspect's safe canvas and clear of its keep-out boxes.
A wider or taller crop can reveal what the original hid; look at every reframed shot on its own.
Labels for AI voice and synthetic data survive every reframe.

nouns.title: Conform and export rules
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call procedure checked before and after rendering.

rules: Conform: every event resolves to a pinned media noun at the plan's frame rate; nothing is offline; the main video track has no gap or overlap; the total equals the planned frames.

Each export profile names its aspect, size, frame rate, codec and profile, chroma, colour tags, audio codec, rate and channels, fast start, edit lists, size and bitrate budgets, loudness target and sidecars.
A web master is H.264 High, 4:2:0, BT.709, constant frame rate, AAC-LC at 48 kHz in stereo, with the moov box first.
A host with a size limit sets the budget; one production capped a 3-minute 1080p cut at 40 MB and raised the encoder's quality factor to fit.
Every delivered file is hashed; the export spec, the conformed list and the render manifests are kept so the cut can be rebuilt.
File names carry the cut, the aspect and the version, never a person's name or a local path.

nouns.title: Template: an edit decision list

value.describes: one version of a cut as events on video and audio tracks: source and record frames, the transition into each, the audio offset of a J or L cut, the lines each shot carries, its new on-screen words, its visual beats and the reason for it
rules: Frames are whole numbers at the list's fps.
A revised list names the version it revises.

value.describes: per shot on the main video track: length, words spoken and their rate, new on-screen words and their reading need, the longest gap between beats, and the pacing rules' verdicts

nouns.title: Template: an audio mix plan

nouns.title: Template: a colour and contrast report

nouns.title: Template: a reframe plan for other aspect ratios

value.describes: one delivery profile per output: aspect, size, frame rate, codec and profile, chroma, colour primaries, audio, fast start, edit lists, size and bitrate budgets, loudness target, sidecars and open captions
rules: Each profile maps to the video QA pack's file spec: faststart, codec, profile, chroma, size, frame rate, colour, audio and budgets.

nouns.title: Template: a conform check before rendering

value.describes: whether every event resolved to a pinned media noun at the plan's frame rate, with offline events, gaps, overlaps and the frame totals

nouns.title: Template: what one revision changed and why
nouns.category_reason: A record of what one revision changed and why, kept beside both versions.

value.describes: the changes from one edit list version to the next, each naming the finding it answers, the issue seen, the change made and the events it touched

nouns.title: Template: a person's lock of the cut

value.describes: a person's decision, after watching the whole cut with sound on the screens named, to lock it or send it back with notes

nouns.title: Edit checks, with one good and six bad edit summaries the validator recomputes
nouns.category_reason: A golden fixture: fixed edit summaries and the recorded results of every check.

value.purpose: Deterministic checks an edit summary passes before a cut is rendered or locked, each shown failing on a bad summary for exactly its own reason.

deterministic_checks.why: Every event resolves to a media noun.
Every event says why it is there.
Sources are noun keys, never a person's local paths.
A revision names each issue seen and each change made.
Only a person locks a cut.
No dissolve joins two frames full of text.

nouns.title: Checklist a person runs before locking a cut
nouns.category_reason: A short checklist a person runs is part of the edit's guardrails.

items: Watch the whole cut at normal speed with sound, once on headphones and once on a phone speaker.
Every shot supports its words, and nothing shows a payoff or a number before the voice reaches it.
No text sits past the frame edge, under a label or inside a dissolve.
Every flagged shot in the pacing report is fixed or accepted with a reason in your own words.
Labels for AI voice and synthetic data are on screen wherever they apply, in every aspect.
Each revision note says what was seen and what changed; earlier versions are still there.
